# Module `webgl`

WebGL 1 and 2 for native/js/odin/web_webgl.js: a context is a host object over a device of its own (native/webgl: a thread in the GPU
process); the script sends it command buffers and waits only for what it has to know. A context that is gone (its canvas freed, its
device lost, the process dead) does nothing and answers -1 or false: these calls also come from a Wasm module of the page with any
numbers, and the command stream is checked on the device's side. In a worker a context is on an OffscreenCanvas.

Exposed to: Window, Worker. Source: `api/webgl.widl`.

## Types

### callback `WebGLNotify`

```
void WebGLNotify(i32 user, i32 kind)
```

What a context has to say: kind 1 it was lost.

### `WebGL_create`

```
u64 WebGL_create(HTMLCanvasElement canvas, u32 flags, WebGLNotify notify, i32 user, out bytes info)
```

A context on a canvas (an element or an OffscreenCanvas). flags: 1 WebGL 2, 2 alpha, 4 depth, 8 stencil, 16 antialias,
32 premultipliedAlpha, 64 preserveDrawingBuffer, 128 failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat. `info`: 8 i32, for the script. 0: refused,
WebGL_createError says why (nothing when the canvas already has a context of another kind).

Host: `WebGL_create :: proc(c: ^Call, canvas: Api_HTMLCanvasElement, flags: u32, notify: u32, user: i32, info: []u8) -> u64`

### `WebGL_upload`

```
i32 WebGL_upload(u64 gl, bytes command, u64 source) raises
```

texImage2D of an element or an ImageBitmap: the command with the source's pixels and size. Raises Security for what the
page may not read. 1: nothing to read yet (an image still loading), the page gets INVALID_VALUE.

Raises: returns an `Error` (see [web](web.md)).

Host: `WebGL_upload :: proc(c: ^Call, gl: u64, command: []u8, source: u64) -> (i32, Api_Error)`
